article.headline: Harry Kane matches appearance record as England routs Czech Republic 3-0
article.summary: England secured a 3-0 Nations League victory over the Czech Republic at Wembley on Tuesday behind two goals from Harry Kane.
article.body:
Harry Kane celebrated his record-equalling 125th international appearance by contributing to every goal in England’s victory. The England captain matched Peter Shilton's all-time cap record, a milestone that stood for 36 years, by scoring twice and providing an assist in a dominant performance at Wembley.

The result reinforces England's standing in the Nations League as they conclude a successful international break under manager Thomas Tuchel. With three wins in four matches and 14 total goals scored, England now requires only one point from their final two games to secure a quarter-final qualification spot.

England took an early lead when Czech defender Vladimir Coufal redirected a Kane cross into his own net in the 27th minute. Kane then doubled the advantage five minutes before half-time, connecting on a cross from Morgan Rogers. The captain completed his brace in the second half, heading in a delivery from Lewis Hall to finalize the scoreline. While Spain leads the group following a 2-1 comeback win against Croatia, England remains in a strong position to advance to the knockout stage. Kane, who now has over 90 international goals, was substituted in the 80th minute.

Following the completion of this international period, the team looks ahead to their remaining group matches where a single point will guarantee their progression in the tournament.

article.headline: Lionel Messi Nets Final Goal As Argentina Cruises Past Benin 3-0
article.summary: Lionel Messi concluded his 21-year international career with a penalty goal and two assists in a 3-0 victory against Benin in Buenos Aires.
article.body:
A giant jersey bearing the word “Gracias” and his iconic No. 10 covered the pitch as 85,000 supporters roared their final approval for the 39-year-old superstar. Before the match even began, Messi wiped away tears as his team bus navigated through massive crowds of well-wishers toward the Monumental Stadium. The stadium paused for a minute-long ovation in the 10th minute of play to honor the player’s career. His final international appearance, dubbed "The Last Tango," concluded with a 71st-minute penalty and a spectacular drone show depicting his image in the night sky.

For football followers, this marks the definitive end of an era for a player widely regarded as the greatest in history. Messi, who holds a record-extending 208 international appearances, leaves behind a legacy defined by his 126 international goals. His departure represents a strategic transition for the Argentina national team, as he explicitly stated that he is making space for young players who now deserve their opportunity to represent the country.

According to The Guardian, the farewell occurred just months after a difficult 1-0 loss to Spain in the World Cup final, an event that saw Messi depart in tears. Reflecting on the timing of his exit, Messi noted to EWN that the physical and emotional toll of the recent World Cup campaign was significant, describing his retirement as the saddest day of his career. Despite the sorrow of leaving the pitch, he confirmed he would transition to supporting the squad from the stands.

The match featured additional goals from Nicolás Otamendi and Nico Paz. Following the final whistle, the veteran forward emphasized that while he would have liked to play for the rest of his life, his time with the national team had reached its natural conclusion.
